plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Free, no credit card. 50K Yeps/month and a daily cap of 1,800 Yeps and 300 executions (reset 00:00 CET). 1 concurrent, no queue, 30 s max execution, 150 MB RAM, 5 MB local disk. Webhooks limited to 1 req/s and 5 req/min. No overage: new executions are refused when Yeps run out. trial_only.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: EUR 119/month = $135.40 at 1.1378 USD/EUR. Includes 15M Yeps (4,166.7 process-hours, = included_usd at the overage rate); then +EUR 0.00001 per extra Yep. Max 10 concurrent, 1 h max execution, 300 MB RAM sandboxes, up to 10 team members.

plans.name: Growth
plans.note: EUR 599/month = $681.54 at 1.1378 USD/EUR. Includes 150M Yeps (41,666.7 process-hours); then +EUR 0.000005 per extra Yep. Max 50 concurrent, 12 h max execution, 600 MB RAM sandboxes, unlimited team members.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Starting at EUR 1,800/month (~$2,048 at 1.1378 USD/EUR); custom limits; negotiated.

caveats: Prices are published in EUR only and converted at 1.1378 USD/EUR (ECB reference 2026-09-28, research/fx.json); the USD invoice amount depends on your card FX. Each plan has its own overage rate, so each regime is tied to one plan. vCPU per process is not published (sizes unsized).
Public list prices rendered in EUR; Yeps are rounded-up seconds of process execution. General JS/Python execution service; self-serve memory only300MB/600MB, not arbitrary8GiB machines.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Yep allowances reset on the 1st of each month (00:00 CET) and do not roll over. On paid plans overage is automatic, invoiced at the plan's fixed per-Yep price, with no published spend cap. All purchases are non-refundable. Payments are in EUR and sales tax/VAT is added on top.

On-premise executors (self-host the execution layer, with the control plane in YepCode cloud) are available on Growth and Enterprise. Full-stack on-premise requires Enterprise. On-prem limits are 'TBD' (sales).
Queue and rate limits: Starter 100 queued executions, 10 HTTP req/s, 25 dependencies, 100 dependency installs/day, start delay p95 < 15 s; Growth 1,000 queued, 50 HTTP req/s, start delay p95 < 3 s.

fleet.verification: Developer free plan requires no credit card.
fleet.tiers: Higher paid plans provide more concurrency; custom enterprise arrangements available.
fleet.notes: Developer: 1 concurrent execution, 300 executions/day, 30 seconds/execution. Queue time is not running concurrency. Paid plan limits and execution credits both matter; no approval SLA specified.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: YepCode provides a temporary directory for storing files during process execution.
snapshot_auto.note: Serverless per-execution model: each process execution runs in a fresh Firecracker microVM with a temporary local disk (5 MB-5 GB by plan) that ends with the execution. Nothing is saved or restored between executions; state lives in YepCode Storage (file API) or Datastore (key-value) that code writes explicitly.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Stops the sandbox on its VM instance and marks the sandbox as killed in the API.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The full public REST API (OpenAPI 3.1) has no snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoints; the new Sandboxes resource only has create, update-timeout and kill. Docs never mention snapshots.

harness_api.quote: In YepCode Cloud: open any process in your team and launch Yep Agent to start prompting against your workspace.
harness_api.note: Yep Agent is YepCode's own coding agent (OpenCode running in a Firecracker microVM, per the 'Making Of' blog), but it is only reachable from the web UI and the /ai landing. The REST API, JS/Python SDKs and CLI have no endpoints to start it, send prompts or stream its events. The MCP server exposes run_code/process tools to external agents, which is the reverse direction.

ingress_rules.quote: HTTP basic authentication for exposed public ports: user:credential.
ingress_rules.note: Undocumented outside the OpenAPI spec: POST /sandboxes takes publicHttpPorts ('List of public HTTP ports to expose.') and publicHttpPortsBasicAuth, so you choose which ports are exposed and can put basic auth in front of them. Regular process executions expose no ports; their webhook endpoints take optional basic auth ('If you don't provide a user and password, no authentication would be needed to start the process', docs/executions/webhooks). No IP allowlists or private URLs documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Subsequently, apiKey will contain the value defined in the team variable regardless of whether it was marked as secured or not. Exercise caution to avoid logging or transmitting it from the code.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are team variables (encrypted at rest, 'secured' flag) injected as environment variables into the sandbox; the code sees the real value. The 'without exposing secret values to the LLM' claim (Yep Agent, run_code MCP tool) means the LLM only writes code that reads env vars, not that a proxy injects credentials.

volume_attach.quote: YepCode allows to store files in the file system used during the execution of a process. The number and size of files is limited based on your plan.
volume_attach.note: Only a per-execution local disk (5 MB Developer, 250 MB Starter, 5 GB Growth, unlimited Enterprise). No attachable volumes; persistent files go to YepCode Storage, an object store used through SDK/REST upload/download calls (max 5/100/1,000 files), not a mount.

volume_shared.quote: File Sharing: Create temporary file storage for sharing between processes
volume_shared.note: YepCode Storage is shared by all processes of a team, read-write, but only through API calls (yepcode.storage.upload/download/list/delete, signed URLs), not mounted as a filesystem. No shared volumes.
